sections.content:
You know *resultar* + adjective from B1 Unit 15 (*El argumento resulta convincente*, *Los personajes resultan convincentes*). In art criticism and exhibition reviews, *resultar* extends beyond simple adjective judgements in three productive patterns:

• Subject + *resultar* + adjective + *de* + infinitive: evaluates how an artwork responds to interpretation (*La obra resulta difícil de descifrar*).
• Impersonal *resultar* + adjective + infinitive (no *de*): judges an action or reaction in general (*Resulta imposible ignorar el claroscuro*). Here the adjective stays masculine singular.
• Indirect object + *resultar* + adjective: attributes the impression to a viewer (*Al espectador le resulta desconcertante la primer salón*), agreeing with the subject (*el salón*).

sections.title: Patterns with resultar in criticism
rows: La serie resulta fácil de recorrer.
The series is easy to walk through. (adj + de + inf)
It is hard to ignore the chiaroscuro. (impersonal: no de)
Al espectador le resulta evocador el silencio.
The silence comes across as evocative to the viewer.
A los visitantes les resultan sobrios los murales.
The murals strike visitors as restrained. (plural subject)

items.spanish: La primera sala resulta muy sobria y evocadora.
items.english: The first room comes across as very restrained and evocative.

items.spanish: Al espectador le resulta desconcertante el contraste entre luz y sombra.
items.english: The contrast between light and shadow strikes the viewer as disconcerting.

items.spanish: Algunas piezas resultan difíciles de descifrar sin leer el texto de la pared.
items.english: Some pieces are difficult to decipher without reading the wall text.

items.spanish: Resulta imposible pasar por alto un proyecto tan audaz.
items.english: It is impossible to overlook such a bold project.

sections.content: English speakers often put *de* before the infinitive in impersonal *resultar* clauses (not *Resulta imposible de ignorar* with the infinitive as the subject: say *Resulta imposible ignorar el claroscuro*). Use *de* only when a concrete subject precedes the verb (*La obra resulta difícil de descifrar*); when the infinitive itself is the subject, omit *de* (*Resulta difícil descifrar la obra*).
